title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Bootstrap inference provides confidence intervals indirect effects without assuming normality. medfit implements three bootstrap methods: Parametric bootstrap: Sample parameter distribution (fast, assumes normality) Nonparametric bootstrap: Resample data refit models (robust, slower) Plugin estimator: Point estimate (fastest, CI) methods return BootstrapResult object consistent structure.

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: examples use bundled, simulated mediation_demo data (see ?mediation_demo): randomized treatment, mediators mediator1 mediator2, outcome, two mediator-outcome confounders, covariate1 covariate2. Every model adjusts covariates.

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: sampling distribution indirect effects (\(\times b\)) typically: Non-normal: Even b normal, product Skewed: Often right-skewed Complex: closed-form distribution general case Bootstrap methods: - Don’t assume normality - Provide accurate coverage (closer nominal 95%) - Handle complex indirect effects (serial mediation, moderated mediation)

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Samples estimated parameter distribution: Extract parameter estimates: \(\hat{\theta} = (\hat{}, \hat{b}, ...)\) Extract covariance matrix: \(\hat{\Sigma}\) Sample \(\theta^*_i \sim N(\hat{\theta}, \hat{\Sigma})\) Compute indirect effect: \(IE^*_i = ^*_i \times b^*_i\) Compute percentile CI bootstrap distribution Fast: model refitting required Appropriate : Parameters approximately normal (large n) Inappropriate : Small samples, non-normal parameters fast (refitting) Reproducible seed Works extracted models (need original data) Assumes multivariate normality parameters May underestimate uncertainty small samples
code: # Fit mediation models fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo) fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo)  # Extract mediation structure med_data <- extract_mediation(   fit_m,   model_y = fit_y,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1" )  # Define statistic function for indirect effect # Parameter names are prefixed by model: m_treatment (mediator model), # y_mediator1 and y_treatment (outcome model) indirect_effect <- function(theta) {   theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"] }  # Parametric bootstrap boot_result <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_result) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   parametric Estimate:   0.3328 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.2073   Upper:   0.4757 summary(boot_result) Summary of BootstrapResult ==========================  Method:    parametric Estimate:  0.3327695 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower: 0.2073406   Upper: 0.475666  Bootstrap Distribution Summary:    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  0.1336  0.2847  0.3288  0.3318  0.3738  0.5785

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Resamples data refits models: Resample data replacement: \(D^*_i\) Refit mediator model \(D^*_i\) Refit outcome model \(D^*_i\) Extract paths: \(^*_i\), \(b^*_i\) Compute indirect effect: \(IE^*_i = ^*_i \times b^*_i\) Compute percentile CI bootstrap distribution Robust: Makes parametric assumptions Appropriate : Small samples, non-normal data, GLMs Gold standard: widely accepted method distributional assumptions Robust outliers Captures full sampling variability Computationally intensive (refits models B times) Requires original data Can slow complex models Speed parallel processing:
code: # Statistic function that refits models on resampled data statistic_fn_refit <- function(boot_data) {   # Fit models on bootstrap sample   fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)   fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)    # Extract and compute indirect effect   med_boot <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,                                 treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")   med_boot@a_path * med_boot@b_path }  # Nonparametric bootstrap (requires original data) boot_np <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = statistic_fn_refit,   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123,   parallel = TRUE,   ncores = 4 )  print(boot_np) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.3328 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.2119   Upper:   0.4850 # Detect available cores ncores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1  # Run in parallel boot_np_par <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = statistic_fn_refit,   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 5000,   parallel = TRUE,   ncores = ncores,   seed = 123 )

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: treatment assigned whole clusters, resample clusters, rows. Pass cluster = method = "nonparametric": draw takes clusters replacement gives every drawn cluster fresh id statistic_fn sees data, cluster drawn twice refit two clusters, one larger one. refit singular warns convergence counts failure: excluded, number failures added warning. warning, appears, reports many draws dropped singular non-convergent refits (cluster-level random intercept can collapse zero resample); interval uses remaining draws, N bootstrap samples print shows many . Resampling members within clusters instead (leaving cluster =) breaks dependence mixed model built . published evidence resampling whole clusters treatment varying within clusters 30 clusters; established design fewer clusters (see Methods Formulas).
code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)  nie_of <- function(d) {   fit <- fit_mediation(     Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = d, treatment = "X", mediator = "M",     engine = "lmer", cluster = "school"   )   unname(nie(fit)) }  boot_cl <- bootstrap_mediation(   nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",   n_boot = 200, ci_level = 0.95, seed = 123 ) Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3 bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or non-convergent refits) boot_cl BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.2093 N bootstrap samples: 197  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:  -0.0038   Upper:   0.5241

code: # Access bootstrap estimates (parametric bootstrap from above) boot_estimates <- boot_result@boot_estimates  # Histogram hist(   boot_estimates,   breaks = 50,   main = "Bootstrap Distribution of Indirect Effect",   xlab = "Indirect Effect (a * b)" )  # Add percentile CI abline(v = boot_result@ci_lower, col = "red", lwd = 2) abline(v = boot_result@ci_upper, col = "red", lwd = 2) abline(v = boot_result@estimate, col = "blue", lwd = 2) # Check for normality qqnorm(boot_estimates) qqline(boot_estimates) # 95% CI c(boot_result@ci_lower, boot_result@ci_upper) [1] 0.2073406 0.4756660 # Change confidence level boot_90 <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.90,   seed = 123 ) c(boot_90@ci_lower, boot_90@ci_upper) # Narrower [1] 0.2251035 0.4455627 # Check if CI excludes zero if (boot_result@ci_lower > 0 || boot_result@ci_upper < 0) {   print("Indirect effect is statistically significant") } else {   print("Indirect effect is not statistically significant") } [1] "Indirect effect is statistically significant"

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: serial mediation (treatment -> mediator1 -> mediator2 -> outcome), indirect effect product chain’s paths, \(\times d \times b\). parametric plugin methods accept SerialMediationData object (ParallelMediationData, InteractionMediationData, JointMediationData, ClusterMediationData) well MediationData. statistic_fn receives named @estimates vector, carries chain’s path aliases , d1, b, c_prime: lm chain estimates equation separately, covariance matrix sets covariances equations zero (see Model Extraction article). avoid assumption, bootstrap nonparametrically resampling data refitting three models:
code: # Fit the chain: each model adjusts for the covariates and every upstream # variable, so the outcome model includes mediator1 as well as mediator2 fit_serial <- function(d) {   extract_mediation(     lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     model_y = lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator2 +                    covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     treatment = "treatment",     mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),     mediator_models = list(       lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)     )   ) } serial_med <- fit_serial(mediation_demo)  # Point estimate of the serial indirect effect (a * d * b) serial_med@a_path * serial_med@d_path * serial_med@b_path [1] 0.07545039 # Parametric bootstrap: draw the chain's paths from N(estimates, vcov) boot_serial_param <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(theta) unname(theta["a"] * theta["d1"] * theta["b"]),   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = serial_med,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial_param) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   parametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0397   Upper:   0.1194 boot_serial <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(boot_data) {     s <- fit_serial(boot_data)     s@a_path * s@d_path * s@b_path   },   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0383   Upper:   0.1187

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Set seed reproducible results:
code: # Same seed = same results boot1 <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 ) boot2 <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 )  # Identical results identical(boot1@boot_estimates, boot2@boot_estimates) [1] TRUE # Different seed = different results boot3 <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 456 ) identical(boot1@boot_estimates, boot3@boot_estimates) [1] FALSE

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: General guidelines: Exploratory: 1000 samples (fast) Publication: 5000+ samples (stable CI) High stakes: 10,000+ samples (stable) Check stability varying n_boot: CIs similar, n_boot sufficient.
code: # Compare different n_boot boot_1k <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 ) boot_5k <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 5000,   seed = 123 ) boot_10k <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 10000,   seed = 123 )  # Compare CIs rbind(   "1K" = c(boot_1k@ci_lower, boot_1k@ci_upper),   "5K" = c(boot_5k@ci_lower, boot_5k@ci_upper),   "10K" = c(boot_10k@ci_lower, boot_10k@ci_upper) ) [,1]      [,2] 1K  0.2073406 0.4756660 5K  0.2134374 0.4685818 10K 0.2113081 0.4674286

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: medfit currently uses percentile bootstrap (simplest, common). Future versions may add: BCa (bias-corrected accelerated): Adjusts bias skewness Studentized bootstrap: Better coverage cases Bayesian bootstrap: Posterior intervals

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: delta method provides asymptotic SE indirect effects: confint(parm = "effects") computes full @vcov (model Cov(, b) exactly zero, outcome equation contains every regressor mediator equation): Bootstrap generally preferred : - Doesn’t assume normality indirect effect - Handles skewness correctly - Provides better coverage
code: # Delta-method 95% CI for the NIE (assumes normality; warns about it) ci_delta <- confint(med_data, parm = "effects")["nie", ] Warning: Normal approximation for NIE may be inaccurate. Consider bootstrap_mediation() for robust inference. # Compare with bootstrap ci_boot <- c(boot_result@ci_lower, boot_result@ci_upper)  rbind(delta = ci_delta, bootstrap = ci_boot) 2.5 %    97.5 % delta     0.2063564 0.4591826 bootstrap 0.2073406 0.4756660

title: medfit Cookbook
text: : inverse-probability weights, case weights independent observations. Pair se_type = "sandwich"; model-based standard errors valid inverse-probability weights. sandwich (HC3) standard errors treat observations independent, handle survey clusters, strata replicate weights. : Getting Started.
code: ps <- glm(treatment ~ covariate1 + covariate2, family = binomial(),           data = mediation_demo) p_t <- fitted(ps) p_m <- mean(mediation_demo$treatment) ipw <- ifelse(mediation_demo$treatment == 1, p_m / p_t, (1 - p_m) / (1 - p_t)) xw <- fit_mediation(   outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,   mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,   data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",   weights = ipw, se_type = "sandwich" ) tidy(xw, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE) # A tibble: 3 × 5   term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> 1 nie      0.335    0.0657   0.206      0.463 2 nde      0.208    0.115   -0.0180     0.433 3 te       0.542    0.119    0.308      0.776

code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n) xc <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",                     mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school") tidy(xc, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE) # A tibble: 5 × 5   term      estimate std_error conf_low conf_high   <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> 1 nie         0.209     0.127  -0.0397      0.458 2 nde         0.0772    0.227  -0.368       0.522 3 te          0.287     0.241  -0.186       0.760 4 own         0.103     0.0543 -0.00323     0.210 5 spillover   0.106     0.0886 -0.0675      0.280 decompose(xc) own spillover       nie 0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444 attr(,"label") [1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation" nie_of <- function(dd) {   unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = dd, treatment = "X",                            mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school"))) } boot_c <- bootstrap_mediation(   nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",   n_boot = 200, seed = 123 ) Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3 bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or non-convergent refits) boot_c BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.2093 N bootstrap samples: 197  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:  -0.0038   Upper:   0.5241

code: set.seed(11) n <- 400 X <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9) ldat <- data.frame(   X = X,   m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) ) ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) syntax <- "   eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3   eta ~ a * X   Y ~ b * eta + cp * X " xs <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",                     mediator = "eta", engine = "native") tidy(xs, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE) # A tibble: 3 × 5   term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> 1 nie      0.169    0.0310    0.108     0.229 2 nde      0.255    0.0487    0.159     0.350 3 te       0.423    0.0445    0.336     0.510 mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b") Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect  data:  a * b = 0 MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

code: base <- "   mediator1 ~ a * treatment   outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment " free <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo) tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "cp == a * b"), mediation_demo) rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b", "cp")], tied = coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")]) a         b         cp free 0.4559961 0.7134287 0.04057666 tied 0.3381172 0.6831633 0.23098930 chain <- "   mediator1 ~ a * treatment   mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + treatment   outcome ~ b * mediator2 + mediator1 + treatment " mbco_sem(fit_sem(chain, mediation_demo), paths = c("a", "d", "b")) Minimum-of-3 likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect  data:  a * d * b = 0 MBCO = 17.557, df = 1, p-value = 2.788e-05

what: 13. Joint significance for a binary or count outcome
title: medfit Cookbook
text: : outcome binary count want know whether mediated path exists, without outcome-scale effect. Test = 0 b = 0 separately take larger p-value (conservative). test likelihood-ratio test binomial Poisson model F test Gaussian, Gamma quasi* model, whose dispersion estimated. : GLM families.
code: d <- mediation_demo d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome)) joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {   one <- function(fit, term) {     known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")     col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"     drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]   }   p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))   c(p, joint = max(p)) } fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d) fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,              data = d, family = binomial()) joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1") a            b        joint 8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

title: Model Extraction
text: extract_mediation() function provides standardized interface extracting mediation structures fitted models. works : lm/glm models (base R) - implemented lavaan SEM models - implemented lmer mixed models (cluster-level treatment, 2-1-1) - implemented fit_sem() native SEM fits (experimental) - implemented Extraction returns S7 class matches structure: MediationData, InteractionMediationData, SerialMediationData, ParallelMediationData, JointMediationData, ClusterMediationData. share one interface (nie(), confint(), tidy(), bootstrap_mediation(), …) across modeling frameworks. Note: quick analysis, consider using med() instead - handles fitting extraction one step. Use extract_mediation() need control already fitted models.

code: library(medfit) Attaching package: 'medfit' The following object is masked from 'package:stats':      decompose # mediation_demo: simulated data bundled with medfit (see ?mediation_demo). # Its covariates confound the mediator-outcome relation, so adjust for them. covs <- c("covariate1", "covariate2")  # Simple way: med() does everything result <- med(data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment",               mediator = "mediator1", outcome = "outcome", covariates = covs) quick(result) NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 % # Advanced way: fit models separately, then extract fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo) fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo) result <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y, treatment = "treatment",                             mediator = "mediator1") quick(result) NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %

what: Extracting from lmer Models: Cluster-Level Treatment
title: Model Extraction
text: treatment assigned whole clusters (example schools) mediator outcome measured individuals (2-1-1 design), fit two linear mixed models lme4::lmer() pass extract_mediation(). returns ClusterMediationData object. outcome model must carry mediator within-cluster deviation plus observed cluster mean (raw mediator plus cluster mean); medfit finds terms value, grand-mean centering scale() work. natural indirect effect \(\, b_B\) (cluster-mean slope), decompose() splits -mediator part spillover part, labeled large-cluster approximation: fit_mediation(engine = "lmer", cluster = ) builds cluster means models , se_type = "kr" adds Kenward-Roger degrees freedom (needs pbkrtest). -cluster warnings, assumptions effect needs formulas Methods Formulas; use bootstrap_mediation(cluster = ) intervals products (Bootstrap).
code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) cdat$M_bar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$M_w <- cdat$M - cdat$M_bar cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * cdat$M_w + 0.6 * cdat$M_bar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)  fit_m <- lme4::lmer(M ~ X + (1 | school), data = cdat) fit_y <- lme4::lmer(Y ~ X + M_w + M_bar + (1 | school), data = cdat) cluster_med <- extract_mediation(   fit_m, model_y = fit_y, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", cluster = "school" ) cluster_med <ClusterMediationData>   X -> M -> Y  (clusters: school)   a = +0.2720   b_within = +0.3796   b_between = +0.7697   c' = +0.0772   NIE (a * b_between) = +0.2093   n = 400 in 40 clusters (sizes 10 to 10)   |   within outcome model, model SEs Estimand and assumptions:   Design: treatment `X` assigned to 40 clusters (`school`, sizes 10 to 10); linear     mixed models with a random cluster intercept, mediator entering through the     observed cluster mean.   - All rows: linear models with no mediator-by-treatment or mediator-by-covariate     products; treatment randomized; clusters intact.   - Own (a * b_within): no unmeasured lower-level M-Y confounding; additive upper-level     confounders are allowed because level-1 covariates are cluster-mean centered.   - Spillover, NIE and NDE: also no unmeasured upper-level M-Y confounding.   - TE: no assumption beyond randomization of the treatment.   - Own/spillover split: a cross-world assumption across individuals in a cluster; no     treatment-induced M-Y confounding.   - Interference only through the observed cluster mean of the mediator and none     between clusters; members missing from the analysis rows are assumed not to drive     their peers' outcomes. nie(cluster_med) Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2093 decompose(cluster_med) own spillover       nie 0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444 attr(,"label") [1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation"

Indirect effect   indirect := a * b    # Total effect   total := c_prime + a * b "  # Fit model fit <- sem(model_syntax, data = mediation_demo)  # Extract mediation structure med_sem <- extract_mediation(   fit,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   outcome = "outcome" )  print(med_sem) MediationData object ====================  Path coefficients:   a (X -> M):        0.5826   b (M -> Y|X):      0.5711   c' (X -> Y|M):     0.2058   Indirect (a*b):    0.3328  Variables:   Treatment: treatment   Mediator:  mediator1   Outcome:   outcome  Model info:   N observations: 400   Converged:      Yes   Source:         lavaan  Residual SDs:   Mediator model:   0.9743   Outcome model:    1.0360 grep("^(m|y)_", names(med_sem@estimates), value = TRUE) [1] "m_treatment" "y_mediator1" "y_treatment" # code: # Parallel model: mediator1 and mediator3 each on the treatment; outcome on both parallel_syntax <- "   mediator1 ~ a1 * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2   mediator3 ~ a2 * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2   outcome   ~ b1 * mediator1 + b2 * mediator3 + c_prime * treatment +     covariate1 + covariate2    # Total indirect effect = sum of per-mediator products   indirect := a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 "  fit_parallel <- sem(parallel_syntax, data = mediation_demo)  med_parallel <- extract_mediation(   fit_parallel,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator3"),   outcome = "outcome" )  print(med_parallel) <ParallelMediationData>   treatment -> {mediator1, mediator3} -> outcome  (2 parallel mediators)     mediator1 a1 = +0.5826   b1 = +0.5686     mediator3 a2 = +0.4761   b2 = +0.2124   Direct (c'): +0.1062   Indirect (sum a_j*b_j): +0.4324   Total: +0.5386   |   n = 400 nie(med_parallel) Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.4324

title: Model Extraction
text: treatment mediator interact, total effect splits four pieces (VanderWeele 2014): controlled direct effect (CDE), reference interaction (INTref), mediated interaction (INTmed), pure indirect effect (PIE), Total = CDE + INTref + INTmed + PIE, NDE = CDE + INTref, NIE = INTmed + PIE. medfit computes decomposition; causal interpretation (requires VanderWeele’s -unmeasured-confounding assumptions) analyst’s responsibility. extract_mediation() returns InteractionMediationData object whenever outcome model carries X:M term. Set reference mediator level m_star (default 0). lm/glm, X:M term detected automatically. mediation_demo’s outcome_int carries treatment mediator1 interaction: tidy() reports four components type = "components" natural effects type = "effects"; glance() adds interaction coefficient m_star: four-way formulas (continuous Y M) CDE = θ₁ + θ₃·m*, INTref = θ₃·(E[M|X=0] − m*), INTmed = θ₃·β₁, PIE = θ₂·β₁, θ₃ interaction coefficient β₁ path. Non-Gaussian outcomes yet supported raise informative error. lavaan interaction enters product variable (column create), model must fit meanstructure = TRUE mediator intercept (needed INTref) estimated. Name product term via interaction: interaction absent (decomposition = "two_way"), extraction falls back standard MediationData — existing two-way workflows unchanged. two paths extract models fit. fit_mediation() can instead delegate fitting regmedint package, implements VanderWeele’s regression-based estimators closed form, hand back medfit classes: return class follows rule extract_mediation(): X:M term formula_y yields InteractionMediationData, absence plain MediationData. Components map regmedint’s output CDE = cde, INTref = pnde − cde, INTmed = tnie − pnie, PIE = pnie. Standard errors come regmedint’s delta method rather medfit’s, analytical — bootstrap needed — reproduce SEs regmedint::summary() reports model. four-way split read reference mediator level \(m^*\): \[\text{CDE} = \theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*\] \[\text{INTref} = \theta_3\,(E[M \mid X = 0] - m^*)\] Set fit_mediation(m_star = ), defaults 0 every engine: two terms shift exactly compensating directions, nde(), nie(), te(), pm() invariant m_star — CDE/INTref split moves. Passing m_star fit treatment--mediator term error, silent -op. engines reach answer different routes. engine = "glm" applies m_star extraction time, coefficients fit; engine = "regmedint" hands value regmedint::regmedint() m_cde argument, closed-form estimator consumes fitting time. two names denote one quantity, m_cde accepted engine_args — use m_star. Everything regmedint-specific reference level goes engine_args: Recognized names interaction, cvar, mreg, yreg, a0, a1, c_cond; replaces value adapter otherwise derive formulas, families, data. Scope. regmedint engine needs numeric 0/1 treatment linear (Gaussian) mediator model; outcome may Gaussian binomial. Outside range regmedint’s closed-form effects stop products regression coefficients MediationData InteractionMediationData defined terms , adapter raises explicit error instead returning object whose numbers disagree nie(). weights se_type = "sandwich" likewise refused rather silently ignored. regmedint suggested package — install install.packages("regmedint").

title: Getting Started with medfit
text: Set boot = TRUE. default parametric bootstrap, fast assumes estimates approximately normal. nonparametric plugin methods, custom statistic, Bootstrap Inference.
code: result_boot <- med(   data = mediation_demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   outcome = "outcome",   covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2"),   boot = TRUE,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 42 )  quick(result_boot) NIE = 0.333  [0.21, 0.464] | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %

title: Introduction to medfit
text: medfit provides unified infrastructure mediation analysis R. offers: ADHD-friendly API: med() quick analysis, quick() instant results Effect extractors: nie(), nde(), te(), pm(), paths() mediation effects Tidyverse integration: tidy() glance() methods tibble workflows Base R generics: coef(), vcov(), confint(), nobs() S7 classes Native SEM engine (experimental): fit_sem() fits model syntax latent mediators linear nonlinear constraints; mbco_sem() tests indirect effect, anova() compares nested fits, tidy(), glance() confint() summarize SEMFit S7-based classes standardized mediation data structures Foundation mediation analysis ecosystem (RMediation, mediationverse) package eliminates code duplication across mediation packages providing shared infrastructure allowing package focus unique methodological contributions.

title: Introduction to medfit
text: medfit defines S7 classes mediation structure: MediationData (simple), InteractionMediationData (simple treatment--mediator interaction), SerialMediationData, ParallelMediationData, JointMediationData (several mediators treatment--mediator products), ClusterMediationData (treatment assigned whole clusters, lmer fits), BootstrapResult. eighth class, SEMFit, holds model fitted syntax native engine (fit_sem(), experimental). three common classes introduced ; see Model Extraction others. Stores simple mediation models (X -> M -> Y): indirect effect computed * b. Use effect extractors: Stores serial mediation models (X -> M1 -> M2 -> … -> Y): two mediators, serial indirect effect * d * b: Design extensibility: 3+ mediators, d_path becomes vector: - 3 mediators: * d21 * d32 * b (product--four) - k mediators: product--(k+1) Stores bootstrap inference results:
code: library(medfit) Attaching package: 'medfit' The following object is masked from 'package:stats':      decompose # Example: Create a MediationData object med_data <- MediationData(   a_path = 0.5,           # X -> M effect   b_path = 0.3,           # M -> Y effect (controlling for X)   c_prime = 0.2,          # X -> Y direct effect   treatment = "X",   mediator = "M",   outcome = "Y",   estimates = c(a = 0.5, b = 0.3, c_prime = 0.2),   vcov = diag(3) * 0.01,  # Covariance matrix   sigma_m = 1.0,          # residual SD of the mediator model   sigma_y = 1.2,          # residual SD of the outcome model   mediator_predictors = "X",   outcome_predictors = c("X", "M"),   data = NULL,   n_obs = 100L,   converged = TRUE,   source_package = "medfit" )  # Print method shows key information print(med_data) MediationData object ====================  Path coefficients:   a (X -> M):        0.5000   b (M -> Y|X):      0.3000   c' (X -> Y|M):     0.2000   Indirect (a*b):    0.1500  Variables:   Treatment: X   Mediator:  M   Outcome:   Y  Model info:   N observations: 100   Converged:      Yes   Source:         medfit  Residual SDs:   Mediator model:   1.0000   Outcome model:    1.2000 # Total Effect (nie + nde) Total Effect (TE): 0.35 pm(med_data)    # Proportion Mediated Proportion Mediated (PM): 0.4286 paths(med_data) # All path coefficients a       b c_prime     0.5     0.3     0.2 # Just a, b, c' # A tibble: 3 × 3   term    estimate std_error   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl> 1 a            0.5        NA 2 b            0.3        NA 3 c_prime      0.2        NA tidy(med_data, type = "effects")  # A tibble: 1 × 6     nie   nde    te    pm  nobs converged   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int> <lgl> 1  0.15   0.2  0.35 0.429   100 TRUE # Standard generics work on medfit objects coef(med_data)               # Path coefficients a       b c_prime     0.5     0.3     0.2 coef(med_data, "effects")    # nie, nde, te nie  nde   te 0.15 0.20 0.35 vcov(med_data)               # Variance-covariance matrix [,1] [,2] [,3] [1,] 0.01 0.00 0.00 [2,] 0.00 0.01 0.00 [3,] 0.00 0.00 0.01 confint(med_data)            # Confidence intervals 2.5 %    97.5 % a       0.304003602 0.6959964 b       0.104003602 0.4959964 c_prime 0.004003602 0.3959964 nobs(med_data)               # Number of observations [1] 100 # Example: Two-mediator serial mediation (X -> M1 -> M2 -> Y) serial_data <- SerialMediationData(   a_path = 0.4,           # code: joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {   one <- function(fit, term) {     known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")     col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"     drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]   }   p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))   c(p, joint = max(p)) } fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d) fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,              data = d, family = binomial()) joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1") a            b        joint 8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

title: medfit: Infrastructure for Mediation Analysis in R
text: treatment assigned whole clusters (schools), use lmer engine (needs suggested lme4; add se_type = "kr" pbkrtest clusters): See Methods Formulas estimand assumptions effect needs. mediator construct measured several indicators, write model syntax. native maximum-likelihood engine experimental needs package:
code: # 40 schools of 10 students, treatment assigned by school set.seed(123) J <- 40 n <- 10 school <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(school), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[school]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n)  fit <- fit_mediation(   Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat,   treatment = "X", mediator = "M",   engine = "lmer", cluster = "school" )  nie(fit)        # a * b_between decompose(fit)  # own-mediator and spillover parts (large-cluster approximation) #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.328 #>        own  spillover        nie #> 0.25763321 0.07036432 0.32799753 # a latent mediator `eta` with three indicators, simulated set.seed(11) n <- 400 X <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9) ldat <- data.frame(   X = X,   m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) ) ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)  syntax <- "   eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3   eta ~ a * X   Y ~ b * eta + cp * X " fit <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",                      mediator = "eta", engine = "native") nie(fit)  mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b")  # minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.1685 #> #>  Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect #> #> data:  a * b = 0 #> MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

title: InteractionMediationData: Mediation with Treatment-Mediator Interaction — InteractionMediationData
text: Path coefficients follow outcome model \(Y = \theta_0 + \theta_1 X + \theta_2 M + \theta_3 XM + \dots\) mediator model \(M = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X + \dots\): a_path = \(\beta_1\), b_path = \(\theta_2\), c_prime = \(\theta_1\), interaction = \(\theta_3\). reference level m_star (\(m^*\)) components \(CDE = \theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*\), \(INTref = \theta_3 (E[M \mid X = 0, \bar c] - m^*)\), \(INTmed = \theta_3 \beta_1\), \(PIE = \theta_2 \beta_1\). \(\theta_3 = 0\) decomposition collapses standard simple mediation (CDE = NDE = \(\theta_1\); INTref = INTmed = 0; NIE = PIE = \(\theta_2\beta_1\)). \(E[M \mid X = 0, \bar c] = \beta_0 + \gamma^\top \bar c\) mediator model's prediction treatment covariate means \(\bar c\). effects treatment contrast 0 1, lm/glm extractor requires Gaussian identity-link models. fit_mediation(engine = "regmedint"), @estimates @vcov also carry regmedint's delta-method covariance four components derived effects.

Define indirect effect function indirect_fn <- function(theta) theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"]  # Plugin estimator (point estimate only, fastest) result_plugin <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_fn,   method = "plugin",   mediation_data = med_data ) print(result_plugin) #> BootstrapResult object #> ====================== #>  #> Method:   plugin #> Estimate:   0.3328 #>  #> (No confidence interval for plugin method)  # \donttest{ # Parametric bootstrap (recommended for most applications) result <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_fn,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 12345 ) print(result) #> BootstrapResult object #> ====================== #>  #> Method:   parametric #> Estimate:   0.3328 #> N bootstrap samples: 1000 #>  #> 95% Confidence Interval: #>   Lower:   0.2163 #>   Upper:   0.4674  # Nonparametric bootstrap (slower but more robust) refit_fn <- function(boot_data) {   fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)   fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)   unname(coef(fit_m)["treatment"] * coef(fit_y)["mediator1"]) }  result_np <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = refit_fn,   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 500,   seed = 12345 ) print(result_np) #> BootstrapResult object #> ====================== #>  #> Method:   nonparametric #> Estimate:   0.3328 #> N bootstrap samples: 500 #>  #> 95% Confidence Interval: #>   Lower:   0.1956 #>   Upper:   0.4865 # }  # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) { # Treatment assigned to whole clusters (needs lme4); formulas hold fixed # effects only, the engine adds the random cluster intercept set.seed(1) J <- 30 id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = 6) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(id), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[id]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) # Resample whole clusters. A refit that is singular or does not converge is # dropped, and the warning counts how many were nie_of <- function(d) {   unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = d, treatment = "X",                            mediator = "M", engine = "lmer",                            cluster = "school"))) } result_cluster <- bootstrap_mediation(   nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",   n_boot = 20, seed = 1 ) print(result_cluster) } #> Warning: 3 bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or non-convergent refits) #> BootstrapResult object #> ====================== #>  #> Method:   nonparametric #> Estimate:   0.2927 #> N bootstrap samples: 17 #>  #> 95% Confidence Interval: #>   Lower:   0.0631 #>   Upper:   0.5778 # }

title: Decomposition of a Mediation Effect — decompose
text: 0/1 treatment, outcome model \(Y = \theta_0 + \theta_1 X + \theta_2 M + \theta_3 X M + \dots\), mediator model \(M = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X + \dots\), reference mediator level \(m^*\): $$CDE = \theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*$$ $$INTref = \theta_3 (E[M \mid X = 0, \bar c] - m^*)$$ $$INTmed = \theta_3 \beta_1$$ $$PIE = \theta_2 \beta_1$$ \(NDE = CDE + INTref\), \(NIE = INTmed + PIE\), \(TE = NDE + NIE\). \(E[M \mid X = 0, \bar c]\) mediator model's prediction treatment covariate means.

code: # \donttest{ # Extract the mediation structure from fitted lm models, using the # simulated mediation_demo data bundled with medfit fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo) fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo) med_data <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,                               treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1") # }  # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) { # Treatment assigned to whole clusters (needs lme4); formulas hold fixed # effects only, the engine adds the random cluster intercept set.seed(1) J <- 30 id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = 6) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(id), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[id]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) # The outcome model carries the mediator as its within-cluster deviation # plus the observed cluster mean cdat$M_bar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$M_w <- cdat$M - cdat$M_bar fit_m <- lme4::lmer(M ~ X + (1 | school), data = cdat) fit_y <- lme4::lmer(Y ~ X + M_w + M_bar + (1 | school), data = cdat) cluster_med <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y, treatment = "X",                                  mediator = "M", cluster = "school") nie(cluster_med) } #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2927 # }

title: medfit 0.3.0 (2026-06-06)
text: MediationData now carries GLM family/link mediator outcome models new family_m family_y properties (populated lm/glm lavaan extractors; default NULL treated Gaussian). lets scale-free estimands probmed::pmed() simulate non-Gaussian potential outcomes correct (e.g. logit) scale rather discarding link. Backward compatible: existing constructors omit families continue work. New S7 class InteractionMediationData simple mediation treatment--mediator interaction (X:M outcome model), carrying VanderWeele’s (2014) four-way decomposition total effect controlled direct effect (CDE), reference interaction (INTref), mediated interaction (INTmed), pure indirect effect (PIE), NDE = CDE + INTref NIE = INTmed + PIE. class validator enforces aggregate identities path ties (INTmed = theta3 * beta1, PIE = theta2 * beta1, CDE = theta1 + theta3 * m*), inconsistent decomposition rejected construction. Effect extractors (nie, nde, te, pm) methods new class, plus new decompose() generic returning four components derived effects. extract_mediation() now builds InteractionMediationData lm/glm fits whose outcome model contains X:M term. new decomposition argument ("auto" default / "four_way" / "two_way") controls detection, m_star sets reference mediator level. Continuous (Gaussian) mediator outcome supported (non-Gaussian models error clear message); -interaction path unchanged. companion confint() method gives delta-method intervals parm = "paths", "components" (four-way CDE/INTref/INTmed/PIE), "effects" (NDE/NIE/TE). extract_mediation() also builds InteractionMediationData lavaan fit. interaction enters product variable named via interaction argument, model must fit meanstructure = TRUE (mediator intercept needed INTref). SEM estimated jointly, extracted @vcov carries full joint covariance paths. “treatment-mediator interaction” section added extraction article. New S7 class ParallelMediationData parallel mediation (X -> M_j -> Y independent mediators j = 1..k). total indirect effect sum per-mediator products, sum(a_j * b_j). Completes structural trio alongside MediationData (simple) SerialMediationData (serial). Effect extractors (nie, nde, te, pm, paths) methods new class; paths() returns interleaved a1, b1, a2, b2, ..., c_prime. extract_mediation() now builds ParallelMediationData lm/glm fits: pass per-mediator models via mediator_models new structure = "parallel" argument. structure = "auto" (default) infers serial vs parallel mediator models’ predictors, defaulting serial unless positive evidence parallel structure. returned @vcov named a1, b1, ..., c_prime; b_j (jointly fit outcome model) keep mutual covariances cov(b_j, c'), a_j (separate mediator regressions) independent. extract_mediation() also builds ParallelMediationData single lavaan sem() fit: pass mediator vector (optionally) structure = "parallel". structure = "auto" infers parallel vs serial SEM’s regression rows. system estimated jointly, extracted @vcov preserves -diagonals — including cov(a_j, b_j) cov(a_j, a_{j'}) — SEs reflect full joint covariance (differ block-diagonal lm/glm engine identical data). New confint() method ParallelMediationData (parm = "paths" "effects"). indirect-effect variance uses delta method full {a1, b1, ..., ak, bk} covariance block, correlated b_j handled correctly; method = "boot" directs bootstrap_mediation().
